resources.string: All languages of the game are built in (no language pack needed); the change applies at the next start of the game.
The game picks its own render resolution for each Switch mode; the display hardware scales the picture to the screen.
Widescreen: wider view at the sides (next launch)

Widescreen renders the game in the shape of the screen (e.g. 2000×900 docked, 1600×720 handheld): more of the world at the sides, the HUD at the screen edges. It needs a restart of the game; until then the picture keeps 16:9 with bars.
Widescreen: stretch loading screens to the whole screen
30 saves battery and heat. The game itself runs at 60 (as on the Switch); higher limits are not offered.
In use now: system driver (%1$s did not start)
Driver packages (adrenotools: meta.json + .so, or a .zip) go to Download/DivinityOriginalSin2Mobile/drivers/.
Faded: the ⚙ button is drawn at the opacity below until it is pressed; it stays in the same place.
The last launches with %1$s ended before the first frame: the system driver is used.
Driver %1$s did not start (%2$s): the system driver is used.

Touch: the left stick appears under your thumb in the lower left; touch and hold the world to walk there, double-tap to evade toward the point; skills on the right (A primary, B, X, Y, R, ZR), L = potion. The MENU button switches to menu gestures: swipe to move the selection, tap = A, long press = hold A, B stays a button.
About once a second the skill icons are copied from the HUD of the game (bottom left) onto the buttons with the same letter; a button whose letter the HUD does not show keeps its plain look.
Saves this dialog, then drag the controls on the screen; Reset layout puts them back. Positions are kept for each layout separately.
Touch layout: walking to the finger
Hero height on the picture (from the top): %1$d%%
The hero walks from his spot on the screen toward the held finger. Depth correction makes up for the slanted camera: lower values turn touches above or below the hero more toward straight up or down.
Drag a control to move it
Sticks appear only under the finger (as D2R Mobile)
Drag a button (its group moves as one); a second finger resizes it; − / + with none chosen resize all; Hide takes the chosen out of the game
Drag a button (every button on its own); a second finger resizes it; − / + with none chosen resize all; Hide takes the chosen out of the game

Drag a control (the ABXY diamond and the d-pad move as one); a second finger resizes it; − / + with none chosen resize all; Hide takes the chosen out of the game; Add… brings back L3 / R3 and hidden ones
Drag a control (every button on its own); a second finger resizes it; − / + with none chosen resize all; Hide takes the chosen out of the game; Add… brings back L3 / R3 and hidden ones

Restart the game now to apply the mods?
The game will start with the enabled mods (modded games use their own save folder).
The game will start without mods, with your normal saves.
Put PC Divinity: Original Sin 2 mods (.MOD files) into %s. Ticked mods are loaded from top to bottom: a mod lower in the list wins over the ones above it where they change the same file.

Changes apply at the next start of the game (close it and open it again). While any mod is on, the game uses a separate save folder (a copy of your saves made the first time); your normal saves are not changed.
No .MOD files in the folder yet.
Local multiplayer works between phones on the same Wi-Fi or hotspot. Nothing is opened until you host or look for a local game.
Thermal mode (lower the quality when the phone heats up)
With a gamepad connected, the column is
Touch as mouse (experiment): tap = click, hold = right click, pinch = zoom
Lowest 3D resolution it may drop to (per side; it holds the target but never goes below this)
Switch: the console interface and the on-screen gamepad; taps on the game do nothing
Hybrid: the console interface + touch (as before)
Touch (experiment): like on the iPad, no on-screen gamepad; a press on a real gamepad brings the console interface
Menus change at once, the game screen after the next load or the return to the main menu.

60 is the default. 30 saves battery and heat. 90 and 120 are shown only when the screen has such a mode; above 60 and «No limit» are experimental: more heat and battery, and the game keeps its normal speed. Loading screens and videos stay at 60.
Up to %1$d characters; empty = the default (%2$s)
Off: walk by tapping the floor
Without it: tap the floor to walk, pinch to zoom, two fingers left / right turn the camera
Off: swipe with one finger or two fingers to turn, pinch to zoom

Simplified graphics for more FPS, like lowering the settings on a PC. Off = the picture as the game draws it. The 3D resolution and FSR upscaling are on the main page (Screen and resolution). Applies on the next launch.

Light: hard to notice (slightly shorter model detail distance, a lighter shadow edge filter). Medium: plus simpler distant models, smaller shadow maps, slightly softer distant textures, 4x angle filtering, at most 4 lamps on one spot. Maximum: plus no glow, no distant shadows, softer distant textures, 2x angle filtering, at most 2 lamps on one spot. Changing any row below makes it Custom.
No edge smoothing at 100 % (jagged edges; with a lower 3D resolution the upscaling replaces it)
Smaller shadow maps 512 instead of 768 (softer shadows)
No distant shadows (the far shadow cascade is not drawn; noticeable)
Model detail and draw distance (lower = simpler models sooner, distant objects vanish sooner)
Lamps and torches lighting one spot at most (all = as the game)
Switch mode (the game window; the interface is drawn at this size)

Docked and Handheld are the two Switch modes. The window shown here is the size the interface is drawn at; Docked uses the screen\'s own resolution. The 3D world has its own resolution below, for each mode.
Dynamic (DRS): the game picks it to hold the frame rate

Only the 3D world is scaled: the interface and text always stay at the full window size and stay sharp. A lower percentage gives more FPS and less heat, but a softer 3D picture. Each Switch mode keeps its own choice; this shows the mode picked above. Every choice here applies at once, without a restart.

Instead of a fixed resolution, the dynamic one will be used: the game lowers the 3D resolution by itself whenever the phone cannot hold the target frame rate, and raises it again when it can, but never below the lowest resolution chosen below (now %1$d %%). The interface always stays sharp. Applies at once.
Sharp upscaling FSR 1 instead of a blurry stretch (works only while the 3D is below 100 %, fixed or dynamic; best with Sharpening on)
